66500.q: What is allowed in liberal communities, unlike in Orthodox ones?
66500.e: In Liberal Judaism women and men have the same religious rights. That is why there are women rabbis.
66500.m: In liberal communities women can become rabbis.

66501.q: What did Regina Jonas from Berlin become in 1935, as the first woman in the world?
66501.e: Regina Jonas was ordained as a rabbi in Offenbach am Main in 1935. She was murdered in Auschwitz in 1944.
66501.m: Regina Jonas was the first woman rabbi in the world.

66502.q: In which Swiss city is the liberal Jewish community Or Chadasch?
66502.e: The name Or Chadasch means “new light”. It is one of the largest liberal Jewish communities in Switzerland.
66502.m: The liberal Jewish community in Zurich is called Or Chadasch.

66503.q: In which canton are Endingen and Lengnau?
66503.e: The two neighbouring villages are in the district of Zurzach in the canton of Aargau. They are among the most important places of Jewish history in Switzerland.
66503.m: Endingen and Lengnau are in the canton of Aargau.

66504.q: In which valley are Endingen and Lengnau?
66504.e: Endingen and Lengnau lie on the Surb, a tributary of the Aare. That is why people often speak of the “Surbtal Jews”.
66504.m: Endingen and Lengnau are in the Surbtal.

66505.q: What was special about Endingen and Lengnau from 1776?
a: Only there were Jews allowed to live in Switzerland
The only church in Aargau stood there
66505.e: From 1776 Jews in Switzerland only had the right to live in these two villages. But they were not allowed to do many jobs or own land.
66505.m: From 1776 Jews in Switzerland were only allowed to live in Endingen and Lengnau.

66506.q: What is special about the Jewish cemetery between Endingen and Lengnau?
a: It is the oldest existing one in Switzerland
It is the largest cemetery in Europe
It is on a mountain top
It is only open at night
66506.e: The cemetery was laid out around 1750 and is today the oldest Jewish cemetery in Switzerland that still exists. It is a protected monument.
66506.m: The oldest Jewish cemetery in Switzerland lies between Endingen and Lengnau.

66507.q: Where did the Jews from Endingen and Lengnau bury their dead before 1750?
a: On an island in the Rhine
66507.e: Before that they had to bury their dead on the “Judenäule”, a small island in the Rhine near Koblenz in Aargau. Floods often destroyed the graves there.
66507.m: Before 1750 the graves of the Jews from Endingen and Lengnau were on an island in the Rhine.

66508.q: What does the synagogue in Endingen have that synagogues hardly ever have?
a: A bell tower with a cross
66508.e: Endingen had no church with a tower, so the synagogue from 1852 carries the village clock. That is very unusual for a synagogue.
66508.m: The synagogue in Endingen carries the village clock.

66509.q: Which Jewish place of worship stands in Lengnau and in Endingen?
66509.e: Both villages have a synagogue from the 19th century. The synagogue in Lengnau was consecrated in 1847.
66509.m: There are synagogues in Endingen and Lengnau.

66510.q: From which year were Jews allowed to settle freely anywhere in Switzerland?
66510.e: A popular vote in 1866 gave Jews the right to settle freely. After that many families moved from Endingen and Lengnau to towns such as Baden and Zurich.
66510.m: Since 1866 Jews have been allowed to live anywhere in Switzerland.

66511.q: According to Hindu tradition, how many Vedas are there?
66511.e: The four Vedas are called the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.

66512.q: Which Veda is considered the oldest?
66512.e: The Rigveda is a collection of hymns and was probably composed from around 1500 to 1200 BC.
66512.m: The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas.

66513.q: What does the word “Veda” mean when translated?

66514.q: How were the Vedas passed on for many centuries?
66514.e: Priests learnt the verses exactly by heart and passed them on orally to pupils, long before they were written down.
66514.m: For a long time the Vedas were only passed on orally.

66515.q: What does the Rigveda mainly contain?
66515.e: The Rigveda is made up of over a thousand hymns praising gods such as Indra, Agni and Varuna.
66515.m: The Rigveda is a collection of hymns.

66516.q: Which god of fire is often called upon in the Vedas?
66516.e: Agni is the god of fire and, according to Vedic belief, carries the offerings to the gods.
66516.m: Agni is the Vedic god of fire.

66517.q: In which ancient language were the Vedas composed?
66517.e: The Vedas are composed in an old form of Sanskrit. Sanskrit is the holy language of Hinduism.
66517.m: The Vedas are composed in Sanskrit.

66518.q: What role does Brahma have in the divine trinity, the Trimurti?
66518.e: In the Trimurti, Brahma creates the world, Vishnu preserves it and Shiva destroys it so that something new can arise.
66518.m: Brahma is seen as the creator of the world.

66519.q: How many heads does Brahma have in most images?
66519.e: Brahma is usually shown with four heads looking in all four directions.

66520.e: Brahma's mount is the hamsa, a swan or goose, a sign of purity and wisdom.

66521.e: Saraswati is the goddess of wisdom, music and the arts and belongs with Brahma.
66521.m: Saraswati is the goddess of wisdom and Brahma's companion.

66522.q: According to a well-known legend, what was Brahma born from?
66522.e: According to the legend, a lotus flower grows from Vishnu's navel, and Brahma appears in it.
66522.m: Brahma appeared in a lotus flower.

66523.q: Why are there only very few temples for Brahma in India?
a: He is seen as a demon
66523.e: Although Brahma is important as the creator, he is hardly worshipped in everyday life; Vishnu and Shiva have many more followers.
66523.m: Brahma is rarely worshipped in temples of his own.

66524.q: In which place in Rajasthan is the most famous Brahma temple?
66524.e: The Brahma temple in Pushkar by the holy lake is one of the few large temples for Brahma.
66524.m: The best-known Brahma temple is in Pushkar.

66525.q: What role does Vishnu have in the Trimurti?
66525.e: Vishnu keeps the order of the world and steps in when evil gets the upper hand.
66525.m: Vishnu is the preserver of the world.

66526.q: According to Hindu belief, what does Vishnu do when evil becomes too strong on earth?
a: He comes to earth in a new form
66526.e: Vishnu appears on earth again and again in new forms to save the good. These appearances are called avatars.
66526.m: Vishnu comes to earth in different forms.

66527.e: Garuda is a mighty bird, half eagle and half human, and carries Vishnu through the air.

66528.q: According to mythology, what does Vishnu rest on in the cosmic ocean?
66528.e: Vishnu rests on the many-headed snake Shesha, which floats on the cosmic ocean.
66528.m: Vishnu rests on the world snake Shesha.

66529.e: Lakshmi is the goddess of good fortune and wealth and Vishnu's wife.

66530.q: Which disc-shaped weapon does Vishnu hold in one hand?
66530.e: The Sudarshana Chakra is a spinning throwing disc and one of Vishnu's symbols.
66530.m: Vishnu carries a throwing disc, the chakra.

66531.q: Apart from the chakra, what does Vishnu often hold in another hand?
66531.e: Vishnu carries a conch shell, the shankha, whose sound is meant to drive away evil; he also has a mace and a lotus.
66531.m: The conch shell is a symbol of Vishnu.

66532.q: Which well-known heroes are seen in Hinduism as appearances of Vishnu?
66532.e: Krishna and Rama are seen as avatars, that is earthly appearances of Vishnu. Those who worship Vishnu as the highest god belong to Vaishnavism.
66532.m: Krishna and Rama are appearances of Vishnu.

66533.q: What role does Shiva have in the Trimurti?
66533.e: Shiva destroys the old so that something new can arise; that is why he is also seen as a renewer.
66533.m: Shiva destroys so that something new can arise.

66534.q: Which three-pointed weapon does Shiva carry?
66534.e: The trident is called the trishula and is Shiva's best-known symbol.

66535.e: The white bull Nandi is Shiva's mount; his statue often stands in front of Shiva temples.
66535.m: Shiva rides on the bull Nandi.

66536.q: What does Shiva have on his forehead in many pictures?
66536.e: Shiva's third eye stands for insight; according to the legend, when he opens it, it can burn everything up.
66536.m: Shiva has a third eye on his forehead.

66537.q: What does Shiva do in his form as Nataraja?
66537.e: As Nataraja, King of Dance, Shiva dances in a ring of fire the dance that destroys and recreates the world.
66537.m: As Nataraja, Shiva is the King of Dance.

66538.q: According to the legend, which holy river flows from Shiva's hair?
66538.e: Shiva caught the goddess Ganga in his hair so that her fall from heaven would not destroy the earth.
66538.m: According to the legend, the Ganges flows from Shiva's hair.

66539.q: According to belief, in which mountain range does Shiva live?
66539.e: Mount Kailash in the Himalayas in Tibet is seen as Shiva's home and is an important place of pilgrimage.
66539.m: According to belief, Shiva lives in the Himalayas.

66540.q: Why does Shiva have a blue throat in some pictures?
66540.e: Shiva drank the world poison that came out when the ocean of milk was churned, and so saved the world; it turned his throat blue.
66540.m: Shiva's blue throat comes from the poison he drank for the world.

66541.q: What does the word “avatar” mean in Hinduism?
66541.e: An avatar is a form in which a god comes down to earth to restore order.
66541.m: An avatar is the descent of a god to earth.

66542.q: How many main avatars of Vishnu does the best-known list count?
66542.e: The well-known list of the ten avatars is called the Dashavatara.
66542.m: According to the best-known list, Vishnu has ten main avatars.

66543.q: As his first avatar, Matsya, as which animal did Vishnu save people from a flood?
66543.e: As the fish Matsya, Vishnu warned the forefather Manu about the great flood and pulled his boat to safety.
66543.m: Vishnu's first avatar, Matsya, was a fish.

66544.q: In which form did Vishnu, as Kurma, carry a mountain on his back?
66544.e: As the tortoise Kurma, Vishnu held up the mountain with which gods and demons churned the ocean of milk.
66544.m: As the tortoise Kurma, Vishnu carried a mountain.

66545.q: What does Narasimha, an avatar of Vishnu, look like?
66545.e: Narasimha is a man-lion; he defeated the demon king Hiranyakashipu and protected his devout son Prahlada.
66545.m: Narasimha is half man and half lion.

66546.q: How did the dwarf Vamana cross the whole world?
66546.e: Vamana asked the demon king Bali for as much land as he could measure in three steps, and then grew to giant size.
66546.m: The dwarf Vamana crossed the world in three steps.

66547.q: According to belief, which avatar of Vishnu is still to appear in the future?
66547.e: Kalki is meant to appear on a white horse at the end of the present age and put an end to evil.
66547.m: Kalki is the future avatar of Vishnu.

66548.q: Which two very popular gods are seen as avatars of Vishnu?
66548.e: Rama is the seventh and Krishna the eighth avatar of Vishnu; both are especially worshipped all over India.
66548.m: Rama and Krishna are avatars of Vishnu.

66549.q: In which ancient language of India was the Ramayana composed?
66549.e: The Ramayana is an epic in Sanskrit. It is credited to the sage Valmiki.
66549.m: The Ramayana is an ancient epic in Sanskrit.

66550.q: What is the name of Rama's wife in the Ramayana?
66550.e: Sita is Rama's wife; her kidnapping sets off the main story of the epic.

66551.q: Who kidnaps Sita in the Ramayana?
66551.e: Ravana, the demon king of Lanka, carries Sita off to his kingdom. This starts the great battle of the epic.
66551.m: The demon king Ravana kidnaps Sita.

66552.q: For how many years does Rama have to go into exile in the forest?
66552.e: Because of a promise made by his father, Rama has to live in the forest for 14 years; Sita and his brother Lakshmana go with him.
66552.m: Rama lives in exile for 14 years.

66553.q: Which monkey god helps Rama find Sita?
66553.e: Hanuman leaps over the sea to Lanka, finds Sita and helps in the battle against Ravana.
66553.m: The monkey god Hanuman is Rama's loyal helper.

66554.q: Who is Rama in the Ramayana?
66554.e: Rama is the eldest son of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya in northern India.

66555.q: According to the Ramayana, how many heads does Ravana have?
66555.e: Ravana is shown with ten heads, which stand for his great learning and power.

66556.q: What is often burnt at the festival of Dussehra in northern India?
66556.e: Dussehra celebrates Rama's victory over Ravana; huge Ravana figures are burnt with fireworks.
66556.m: At Dussehra figures of Ravana are burnt.

66557.q: Which country does the great epic Mahabharata come from?
66557.e: The Mahabharata is one of the most important works of India. It is credited to the sage Vyasa.

66558.q: What kind of head does the god Ganesha have, who according to the legend wrote down the Mahabharata?
66558.e: Ganesha is the god with an elephant's head. According to the legend, he wrote down the whole epic without a break while Vyasa recited it.
66558.m: Ganesha with the elephant's head wrote down the Mahabharata.

66559.q: What is the Mahabharata famous for, among other things?
a: It is one of the longest epics in the world
It is the shortest poem in India
66559.e: With about 100,000 couplets, the Mahabharata is much longer than the Iliad and the Odyssey put together.
66559.m: The Mahabharata is one of the longest epics in the world.

66560.q: How many brothers make up the Pandavas in the Mahabharata?
66560.e: The five Pandava brothers are Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva.

66561.q: Who do the Pandava brothers fight against in the Mahabharata?
66561.e: The Kauravas are the hundred sons of the blind King Dhritarashtra and cousins of the Pandavas. The quarrel over the kingdom leads to war.
66561.m: The Pandavas fight their cousins, the Kauravas.

66562.q: Who wins the great battle in the Mahabharata?
a: Nobody, it ends in a draw
66562.e: The deciding battle on the field of Kurukshetra ends with victory for the Pandavas.
66562.m: The Pandavas win the great battle.

66563.q: Roughly how long does the great battle in the Mahabharata last?
66563.e: The battle of Kurukshetra lasts 18 days and ends with victory for the Pandavas.
66563.m: The battle in the Mahabharata lasts 18 days.

66564.q: In the Mahabharata, which god drives the chariot of the archer Arjuna?
66564.e: Krishna serves as Arjuna's charioteer and gives him important teachings before the battle.

66565.q: To which god is the city of Varanasi especially dedicated?
66565.e: Varanasi is seen as Shiva's city; the Kashi Vishwanath Temple is one of his most important temples.
66565.m: Varanasi is the holy city of Shiva.

66566.q: What are the wide stone steps on the riverbank in Varanasi called?
66566.e: The ghats are steps that lead down to the Ganges; believers bathe and pray there.
66566.m: The riverbank steps in Varanasi are called ghats.

66567.q: On which holy river does Varanasi lie?
66567.e: Varanasi lies on the Ganges, the holiest river of the Hindus. The city is also called Kashi, “the shining one”.
66567.m: Varanasi lies on the holy river Ganges.

66568.q: What happens at ghats such as the Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi?
66568.e: At the Manikarnika Ghat fires burn almost without stopping, on which the dead are cremated.
66568.m: The dead are cremated at the Manikarnika Ghat.

66569.q: Why do many Hindus want to die in Varanasi?
a: They hope to be freed from the cycle of rebirth
66569.e: According to belief, whoever dies in Varanasi is freed from the cycle of rebirths.
66569.m: Whoever dies in Varanasi hopes to be set free.

66570.q: What do priests do every evening by the Ganges in Varanasi?
a: A fire ceremony with oil lamps
66570.e: At the Ganga Aarti priests swing large oil lamps to chants and bells to honour the river.
66570.m: Every evening priests honour the Ganges with a fire ceremony.

66571.q: In which part of India is Varanasi?
a: On an island in the sea
66571.e: Varanasi is in the north of India in the state of Uttar Pradesh, on the plain by the Ganges.
66571.m: Varanasi is in the north of India.

66572.q: Apart from Hinduism, for which religion is the area around Varanasi also very important?
66572.e: In Sarnath, only about 10 kilometres from Varanasi, the Buddha gave his first teaching, according to tradition.
66572.m: The Buddha gave his first teaching near Varanasi.

66573.q: What does samsara mean in Hinduism?
a: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
66573.e: Samsara is the cycle in which the soul is born again and again in a new body after death.
66573.m: Samsara is the cycle of rebirths.

66574.q: According to Hindu belief, what mainly decides the next birth?
66574.e: Good and bad deeds leave effects, called karma, and these influence the next life.

66575.q: What does the Sanskrit word “karma” literally mean?
66575.e: Karma means “deed”; the idea is that every action has consequences for the future.

66576.q: According to Hindu belief, what can you be reborn as?
a: Only as a plant in the forest
66576.e: According to belief, depending on its karma the soul can be reborn as a human, an animal or in other forms of existence.
66576.m: According to belief, you can also be reborn as an animal.

66577.q: Which other religion also has the cycle of rebirth?
66577.e: Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism also teach a cycle of rebirths.
66577.m: Buddhism also teaches the cycle of rebirth.

66578.q: In Hinduism, what is liberation from the cycle of rebirths called?
66578.e: Moksha means “liberation”. According to Hindu belief, whoever reaches it is no longer reborn.
66578.m: Moksha is liberation from the cycle of rebirths.

66579.q: What does a well-known image from Hinduism compare rebirth with?
66579.e: Just as a person takes off old clothes and puts on new ones, so, according to the image, the soul leaves the old body and takes on a new one.
66579.m: According to the image, the soul changes bodies like old clothes.

66580.q: How many varnas, that is main classes, does the classical Indian social order have?
66580.e: The division into four classes is already mentioned in old texts such as the Rigveda. Later the caste system developed from it.
66580.m: The classical order has four varnas.

66581.q: Which class was at the top of the classical order?
66581.e: The Brahmins were priests and scholars and were seen as the highest class.
66581.m: The Brahmins were at the top of the order.

66582.q: What role did the Kshatriyas have?
66582.e: The Kshatriyas were princes and warriors who were meant to protect and rule the land; Rama was a Kshatriya.
66582.m: The Kshatriyas were warriors and rulers.

66583.q: What roles did the Vaishyas have in the old Indian order?
66583.e: The Vaishyas were in charge of trade, farming and raising livestock.
66583.m: The Vaishyas were traders and farmers.

66584.q: What do people who used to be shut out as “untouchables” call themselves today?
66584.e: “Dalit” means roughly “oppressed”; these people stood outside the four varnas and were greatly disadvantaged.
66584.m: People once shut out as “untouchables” call themselves Dalits today.

66585.q: Since when has untouchability been banned by the constitution in India?
66585.e: The constitution of the Republic of India came into force in 1950 and bans untouchability.

66586.q: What does the Sanskrit word “varna” literally mean?
66586.e: Varna means “colour”; the word refers to the four large classes of the old order.

66587.q: According to the traditional caste system, how do you become a member of a caste?
66587.e: You are born into a caste, a so-called jati. There are thousands of them.
66587.m: You are born into a caste.

66588.q: What is a guru in Hinduism?
66588.e: A guru guides their pupils on the spiritual path and passes on knowledge.
66588.m: A guru is a spiritual teacher.

66589.q: What does the Sanskrit word “guru” literally mean?
66589.e: “Guru” literally means “heavy” or “weighty”, in the sense of important and venerable.

66590.q: How does a guru traditionally pass on their knowledge?
a: Not at all, it stays secret
66590.e: A guru teaches their pupils in person. This creates a long chain of tradition.
66590.m: Gurus pass on their knowledge to pupils.

66591.q: At which festival do Hindus honour their gurus and teachers?
66591.e: Guru Purnima is celebrated at the full moon in June or July to thank teachers.
66591.m: At Guru Purnima Hindus honour their teachers.

a: A place for spiritual living and learning
66592.e: In an ashram people live and learn together, often with a guru, with meditation and simple work.
66592.m: An ashram is a place for spiritual living.

66593.q: Which Indian freedom fighter founded the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad?
66593.e: Gandhi lived in the Sabarmati Ashram from 1917; from there he set out on the Salt March in 1930.

66594.q: In which country are there especially many ashrams?
66594.e: Ashrams are part of the tradition of Hinduism. Most of them are in India, for example in Rishikesh on the Ganges.

66595.q: What is the teacher you learn from in an ashram called?
66595.e: In Hinduism a guru is a spiritual teacher. In the ashram pupils often live with them.
66595.m: A guru is a spiritual teacher.

66596.e: Navaratri comes from Sanskrit: “nava” means nine, “ratri” means night.

66597.q: In which animal form does the demon fight whom the goddess Durga defeats at Navaratri?
66597.e: Durga fought the buffalo demon Mahishasura for nine nights and defeated him on the tenth day.
66597.m: At Navaratri Durga defeats a buffalo demon.

66598.q: Which animal does the goddess Durga usually ride?
66598.e: Durga is usually shown riding a lion or tiger, with many arms and weapons.

66599.q: What is celebrated on the tenth day after the nine nights of Navaratri?
a: The victory of good over evil
The start of the rainy season
The end of the rice harvest
66599.e: The tenth day is called Vijayadashami or Dussehra and celebrates the victory of good over evil.
66599.m: After Navaratri people celebrate the victory of good over evil.

66600.q: What do dancers strike together in time in the Dandiya dance at Navaratri?
66600.e: In Garba people dance in a circle; in Dandiya they strike colourful wooden sticks together in time. Both dances are especially popular in Gujarat.
66600.m: In Dandiya people strike colourful wooden sticks together.

66601.q: In which season is the most important Navaratri usually celebrated?
66601.e: The great Sharada Navaratri usually falls in September or October.
66601.m: The great Navaratri is usually celebrated in autumn.

66602.q: What do people in West Bengal set up in elaborate festival tents for Durga Puja?
a: Large figures of the goddess Durga
Models of temples made of ice
66602.e: In Kolkata people build elaborate festival tents with large Durga figures for Durga Puja.
66602.m: For Durga Puja people set up large Durga figures.

66603.q: Which country do most Hindus in Switzerland come from?
66603.e: According to the 2000 census, about 81 per cent of the Hindus in Switzerland were Tamils from Sri Lanka.
66603.m: Most Hindus in Switzerland are Tamils from Sri Lanka.

66604.q: Why did many Tamils come to Switzerland from the 1980s onwards?
a: They fled the civil war in Sri Lanka
They were looking for work in mines
66604.e: The civil war in Sri Lanka lasted from 1983 to 2009; many Tamils found refuge in Switzerland.
66604.m: Many Tamils came to Switzerland as refugees from the civil war.

66605.q: Which language do most Hindus from Sri Lanka in Switzerland speak as their mother tongue?
66605.e: Tamil is a very old language with its own script and is spoken in southern India and in the north of Sri Lanka.
66605.m: The mother tongue of many Hindus in Switzerland is Tamil.

66606.q: In which building in Bern has there been a Hindu temple next to prayer rooms of other religions since 2014?
66606.e: In the House of Religions on Europaplatz in Bern several religious communities have their rooms, including a Hindu temple.
66606.m: The House of Religions in Bern houses a Hindu temple.

66607.q: Which god is the Hindu temple in the House of Religions in Bern mainly dedicated to?
66607.e: The temple of the Saivanerikoodam association is mainly dedicated to Shiva, as is usual for many Tamil Hindus.
66607.m: The Hindu temple in Bern is mainly dedicated to Shiva.

66608.q: What was new for Switzerland at the Hindu temple in Bern?
a: It is only open at night
66608.e: The temple in the House of Religions was the first in the Swiss Hindu community to train women as priests.
66608.m: Hindu women priests were trained for the first time in Bern.

66609.q: Where have many Hindu communities in Switzerland set up their temples?
66609.e: Many Hindu communities converted warehouses or factory rooms into temples, for example in Dürnten in the canton of Zurich.
66609.m: Many Hindu temples in Switzerland are in converted halls.

66610.q: What is the first of the Four Noble Truths about?
66610.e: The first truth says that life brings suffering, such as illness, old age and loss.
66610.m: The first Noble Truth speaks of suffering.

66611.q: What does the second Noble Truth name as the cause of suffering?
66611.e: The second truth names “thirst” (tanha), that is greed, craving and clinging, as the cause of suffering.
66611.m: According to the Buddha, suffering comes from craving.

66612.q: What does the third Noble Truth say?
66612.e: The third truth teaches that suffering ends when craving is completely extinguished.
66612.m: When craving is extinguished, suffering ends too.

66613.q: Which path does the fourth Noble Truth name for overcoming suffering?
66613.e: The fourth truth describes the path to the end of suffering: the Eightfold Path.
66613.m: The fourth Noble Truth shows the way out of suffering.

66614.q: According to Buddhist teaching, what is the state in which all suffering has been extinguished called?
66614.e: Nirvana literally means “blowing out”. It refers to the end of greed, hatred and delusion, and so of suffering.
66614.m: In nirvana all suffering is extinguished.

66615.q: Where did the Buddha first proclaim the Four Noble Truths?
66615.e: After his enlightenment the Buddha gave his first teaching to five ascetics in the Deer Park of Sarnath near Varanasi (Benares).
66615.m: The Buddha gave his first teaching in Sarnath.

66616.q: With which profession are the Four Noble Truths often compared?
66616.e: Like a doctor, the Buddha recognises the illness (suffering), names the cause, says that healing is possible and prescribes a treatment (the path).
66616.m: The Buddha deals with suffering like a doctor with an illness.

66617.q: In Buddhism, what is the cycle of birth, death and rebirth called?
66617.e: Samsara is the cycle of rebirths. According to Buddhist teaching, you can be freed from it through enlightenment.
66617.m: Samsara is the cycle of rebirths.

66618.q: What does the term “dukkha” mean in the Four Noble Truths?
66618.e: Dukkha is a basic term of Buddhist teaching and means suffering, dissatisfaction and impermanence.

66619.q: Which part of the Eightfold Path means steadily striving for good and overcoming bad?
66619.e: Right effort means avoiding bad thoughts and patiently developing good qualities.
66619.m: Right effort means working steadily at the good.

66620.q: Which word comes before each part of the Eightfold Path in the usual English translation?
66620.e: The parts are called right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness and right concentration.
66620.m: Each part of the Eightfold Path begins with the word “right”.

66621.q: Which part of the Eightfold Path means deep concentration in meditation?
66621.e: Right concentration (samadhi) is the eighth part. It means a calm, fully collected mind in meditation.
66621.m: Right concentration is deep concentration in meditation.

66622.q: Which religion does the Eightfold Path belong to?
66622.e: The Eightfold Path is a central teaching of the Buddha. It describes how to live well and overcome suffering.
66622.m: The Eightfold Path is a teaching of Buddhism.

66623.q: In Buddhism, where is the Eightfold Path meant to lead?
a: To a long life without work
66623.e: Whoever follows the Eightfold Path is meant to overcome suffering. Buddhists call the highest goal nirvana.
66623.m: The Eightfold Path is meant to free you from suffering.

66624.q: What is meant by “right livelihood” in the Eightfold Path?
a: Doing a job that does not harm others
Earning as much money as possible
66624.e: Right livelihood means earning your money without harming others. For example, arms dealing or cheating are rejected.
66624.m: Right livelihood harms no other living being.

66625.q: Which part of the Eightfold Path means being aware and attentive in the here and now?
66625.e: Right mindfulness means noticing your body, feelings and thoughts in an alert way and without judging. Today it is also known outside Buddhism.
66625.m: Mindfulness means living consciously in the moment.

a: Staying silent as much as possible
66626.e: Right speech means speaking honestly, kindly and sensibly and avoiding lies, slander, harsh words and idle chatter.
66626.m: Right speech is honest and kind.

66627.q: Between which two extremes does the Buddha's Middle Way lie?
66627.e: The Buddha rejected both a life of pleasure and luxury and harsh self-torment. According to his teaching, neither leads to enlightenment.
66627.m: The Middle Way avoids luxury and self-torment.

66628.q: How did Siddhartha Gautama live in his youth?
a: As a prince in a palace
As a fisherman by a river
As a shepherd in the mountains
66628.e: Siddhartha was the son of a prince of the Shakya clan and grew up in the luxury of a palace.
66628.m: Siddhartha grew up in luxury as a prince.

66629.q: What did Siddhartha do before he discovered the Middle Way?
66629.e: For years Siddhartha lived as a strict ascetic and ate almost nothing. He realised that this self-torment did not help him.
66629.m: Strict fasting did not bring Siddhartha enlightenment.

66630.q: According to tradition, what did Siddhartha accept when he gave up his life of self-denial?
66630.e: Tradition tells that a young woman called Sujata brought him rice with milk. After that he carried on meditating with new strength.
66630.m: A bowl of rice pudding ended Siddhartha's fast.

66631.q: According to tradition, what is the tree under which Siddhartha reached enlightenment called?
66631.e: The tree was a sacred fig in Bodh Gaya. It is called the Bodhi tree, which means “tree of awakening”.
66631.m: Siddhartha awoke under the Bodhi tree.

66632.q: Which image is often used to explain the Middle Way?
a: A string that is neither too tight nor too loose
A river that flows faster and faster
A mountain that gets steeper and steeper
A fire that never goes out
66632.e: A story compares the path with the strings of a lute: if they are too tight they snap, if they are too loose they make no sound.
66632.m: Like a well-tuned string, the Middle Way is neither too tight nor too loose.

66633.e: Buddha is a title of honour from Sanskrit and means “the awakened one” or “the enlightened one”. Siddhartha received it after his enlightenment.

66634.q: What can you learn for everyday life from Buddha’s Middle Way?
a: To always have as much as possible
66634.e: Buddha taught that you should neither live in luxury nor torment yourself. Later a Buddhist school was even named after the middle: Madhyamaka.
66634.m: The Middle Way means finding the right balance.

66635.e: Dharma means teaching, chakra means wheel. The Dharmachakra is one of the most important symbols of Buddhism.
66635.m: The Dharmachakra is the wheel of the teaching.

66636.q: What is Buddha’s first sermon after his enlightenment also called?
a: Setting in motion the wheel of the teaching
Sermon on the Mount of the Awakened One
66636.e: According to tradition, with this sermon Buddha “set the wheel of the teaching in motion”, which means he began spreading his teaching.
66636.m: The first sermon set the wheel of the teaching in motion.

66637.q: What do the eight spokes of the wheel of the teaching stand for?
66637.e: The Dharmachakra often has eight spokes. They stand for the Eightfold Path, the way out of suffering according to Buddha’s teaching.
66637.m: The eight spokes stand for the Eightfold Path.

66638.q: Which country’s flag shows a wheel with 24 spokes?
66638.e: In the middle of the Indian flag there is a blue wheel. It comes from an old Buddhist pillar capital.
66638.m: A wheel with 24 spokes decorates the flag of India.

66639.q: Which Indian ruler supported Buddhism in the 3rd century BC and had pillars with a wheel put up?
66639.e: Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya dynasty turned to Buddhism after a bloody war and had inscriptions and pillars set up all over his empire.
66639.m: Emperor Ashoka spread Buddhism in India.

66640.q: What does the hand gesture (mudra) of “turning the wheel of the teaching” show on Buddha figures?
66640.e: In the Dharmachakra mudra, the thumb and index finger of both hands form circles in front of the chest. It stands for teaching.
66640.m: The Dharmachakra mudra shows Buddha teaching.

66641.q: What does the round shape of the Dharmachakra stand for?
66641.e: The circle is seen as a sign of perfection and wholeness. The spokes stand for the Eightfold Path.
66641.m: The circle of the wheel stands for the perfect teaching.

66642.q: What do believers in Tibetan Buddhism turn to “send out” prayers?
66642.e: Prayer wheels are cylinders with mantras inside. One turn counts as much as saying the prayers inside.

66643.e: Theravada means “teaching of the elders”. This school sees itself as the keeper of Buddha’s original teaching.
66643.m: Theravada is the teaching of the elders.

66644.q: In which country did Buddha, whose teaching Theravada follows, live and teach?
66644.e: Buddha lived about 2500 years ago in the north of India. His teachings were later written down in an old Indian language called Pali.
66644.m: Buddha lived and taught in India.

66645.q: What is the collection of Theravada scriptures called, which literally means “three baskets”?
66645.e: The collection is called Tipitaka because it is made of three “baskets”: rules for monks, sermons and philosophical texts.
66645.m: The collection of Theravada scriptures is called the Tipitaka, the three baskets.

66646.q: In which country is Theravada Buddhism the main religion?
66646.e: Theravada is the most important religion above all in Sri Lanka and in several countries of Southeast Asia.
66646.m: Theravada is widespread in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

66647.q: What goal does a Theravada monk aim for?
a: To become as rich as possible
To become king of the country
66647.e: In Theravada, you want to reach nirvana yourself and be freed from the cycle of rebirth. Someone who manages this is called an arahant.
66647.m: In Theravada, people aim for nirvana.

66648.q: What is the other great branch of Buddhism besides Theravada?
66648.e: The two great branches of Buddhism are Theravada and Mahayana. Mahayana means “great vehicle” and is widespread in China and Japan, for example.
66648.m: Theravada and Mahayana are two great branches of Buddhism.

66649.q: What special role do monks play in Theravada?
a: They are seen as role models on the path to nirvana
They sacrifice animals in the temple
66649.e: In Theravada, life in a monastery is very important because it is seen as the best path to liberation. Lay people support the monks with gifts.
66649.m: In Theravada, monks are important role models.

66650.q: What is the Buddhist community of monks and nuns called?
66650.e: Together with Buddha and the teaching (Dharma), the Sangha is one of the “Three Jewels” in which Buddhists take refuge.
66650.m: Buddha, Dharma and Sangha are the Three Jewels.

66651.e: In Sanskrit, Mahayana means “great vehicle”. It wants to carry as many beings as possible to liberation.

66652.q: What is a bodhisattva in Mahayana?
a: A being who wants to help everyone out of compassion
66652.e: A bodhisattva seeks enlightenment but chooses not to enter nirvana until all beings are freed.
66652.m: A bodhisattva helps all beings out of compassion.

66653.q: In which countries is Mahayana Buddhism mainly found?
66653.e: Mahayana spread along the Silk Road to China and from there to Korea, Japan and Vietnam.
66653.m: Mahayana is widespread in East Asia.

66654.q: What does the bodhisattva Guanyin, who is very popular in China, stand for?
66654.e: In India Guanyin is called Avalokiteshvara and in Japan Kannon. He or she represents compassion for all beings.
66654.m: Guanyin is the bodhisattva of compassion.

66655.q: What are holy texts in Buddhism, such as the Heart Sutra, called?
66655.e: Sutras are teaching texts of Buddhism. The Heart Sutra is one of the shortest and best known and is often recited together in East Asia.
66655.m: Holy texts in Buddhism are called sutras.

66656.q: What do followers of Pure Land Buddhism do to be reborn in the Pure Land?
a: They call on the name of the Buddha Amitabha
They go on a pilgrimage to Mecca
66656.e: Followers of the Pure Land trust in the Buddha Amitabha. They call on his name so that they will be reborn in his “Pure Land”.

66657.q: How is Maitreya, the Buddha of the future, often shown in China?
a: As a warrior with a sword
66657.e: Maitreya is seen as the Buddha who is still to come. In China he is often shown as a cheerful, fat monk.
66657.m: Maitreya is the Buddha of the future.

a: Nothing exists firmly and on its own
You are not allowed to own anything
66658.e: The Sanskrit word is shunyata. It means that all things depend on each other and are always changing.

66659.q: From which country did Buddhism come to Tibet?
66659.e: Buddhism came to Tibet from India. According to tradition, it was brought in the 8th century by the master Padmasambhava, whom Tibetans call “Guru Rinpoche”.
66659.m: Buddhism came to Tibet from India.

66660.q: Why was the 14th Dalai Lama awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989?
a: For his non-violent work for Tibet
66660.e: In 1989 the Nobel Committee honoured his non-violent struggle for the freedom of Tibet.
66660.m: The Dalai Lama received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.

66661.q: To which country did the 14th Dalai Lama flee in 1959?
66661.e: After the Tibetan uprising in 1959, the Dalai Lama fled to India. Since 1960 he has lived in the town of Dharamsala, where the Tibetan government in exile is also based.
66661.m: The Dalai Lama has lived in exile in India since 1959.

66662.q: Which famous palace in Lhasa used to be the winter palace of the Dalai Lamas?
66662.e: The Potala Palace towers above Lhasa and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994. Today it is a museum.
66662.m: The Potala Palace in Lhasa was the seat of the Dalai Lamas.

66663.q: What is the best-known mantra of Tibetan Buddhism?
66663.e: The mantra is dedicated to the bodhisattva of compassion. It is spoken, sung and carved into stones.
66663.m: “Om mani padme hum” is the mantra of compassion.

66664.q: What do Tibetan Buddhists turn so that prayers go out into the world?
66664.e: Inside a prayer wheel there are paper rolls with mantras. According to the belief, every turn works like a spoken prayer.
66664.m: Tibetans send prayers into the world with prayer wheels.

66665.q: What is the Dalai Lama for Tibetan Buddhists?
a: A god who lives in heaven
66665.e: The Dalai Lama is the most important spiritual leader of the Tibetans. He belongs to the Gelug school, also called the “Yellow Hats”.
66665.m: The Dalai Lama is the most important teacher of the Tibetans.

66666.q: What are the colourful flags that flutter in the wind in Tibet?
66666.e: Prayer flags are printed with mantras. According to the belief, the wind carries the blessings out into the world.
66666.m: Prayer flags carry blessings away on the wind.

66667.q: According to Tibetan belief, how is a new Dalai Lama found?
a: People search for a child who is seen as his rebirth
The people elect him at the ballot box
His eldest son inherits the role
66667.e: After a Dalai Lama dies, monks look for a child in whom he is believed to have been reborn. Such reborn teachers are called tulkus.
66667.m: A new Dalai Lama is seen as the rebirth of the previous one.

66668.q: Which country does the name “Zen” come from?
66668.e: Zen is the Japanese pronunciation of the Chinese word Chan. The school came from China to Japan in the 12th and 13th centuries.
66668.m: Zen is the Japanese form of Chan Buddhism.

66669.q: What did the word “Zen” originally mean?
66669.e: Through the Chinese word Chan, Zen comes from the Sanskrit word dhyana, which means meditation or deep concentration.

66670.q: What is sitting meditation called in Zen?
66670.e: In zazen you sit still and upright, usually on a round cushion, and focus your attention on your posture and breathing.
66670.m: Zazen is the sitting meditation of Zen.

66671.q: What is a koan in Zen?
a: A puzzling question to think about
66671.e: A well-known koan asks: “What is the sound of one hand clapping?” Such questions are meant to break through your usual way of thinking.
66671.m: A koan is a puzzle that breaks open your thinking.

66672.q: How do you sit during Zen meditation?
66672.e: In zazen you sit still and upright, often for a long time. According to legend, the monk Bodhidharma meditated facing a wall for nine years.
66672.m: In Zen you meditate sitting still and upright.

a: In a tower block in the city
66673.e: Zen monks live in monasteries and temples. There they meditate, work and learn. In Japan there are two large Zen schools, Rinzai and Soto.
66673.m: Zen monks live in monasteries and temples.

66674.q: What is a classic Japanese Zen garden, like the one at the Ryoan-ji temple, made of?
66674.e: In the rock garden of Ryoan-ji in Kyoto, 15 stones lie in raked white gravel. Gardens like this invite you to meditate.
66674.m: Zen gardens are made of gravel and stones.

66675.q: What is sudden enlightenment called in Zen?
66675.e: Satori is the Japanese word for awakening, or recognising your own true nature.

66676.q: What does the Sanskrit word “mandala” mean?
66676.e: Mandala means circle. A mandala is a picture, usually round, with a clear centre.

66677.q: What do Tibetan monks use to make special mandalas?
66677.e: Using thin tubes, monks spend days pouring grains of dyed sand into a detailed picture.
66677.m: Tibetan monks make mandalas out of sand.

66678.q: What happens to a sand mandala once it is finished?
66678.e: The sand is swept together and often scattered into a river. This shows that all things pass away.
66678.m: The destroyed sand mandala shows that nothing lasts for ever.

66679.q: What is a mandala mainly used for in Buddhism?
66679.e: A mandala shows a holy world. Whoever looks at it is led from the outside to the centre and should become calm inside.
66679.m: The mandala is an aid to meditation.

66680.q: Which basic shape do you find inside the circle of many Tibetan mandalas?
66680.e: The square represents a palace whose four gates face the four directions of the compass. In the centre there is usually a deity or a Buddha.
66680.m: Inside the mandala is a palace with four gates.

66681.q: What is usually in the centre of a Buddhist mandala?
66681.e: The centre is the most important point. It shows the main figure, around which everything else is arranged.
66681.m: The most important figure sits in the centre of the mandala.

66682.q: What did the Swiss psychologist C. G. Jung see in a mandala?
a: A picture of the wholeness of the mind
66682.e: Carl Gustav Jung painted mandalas himself and also had patients paint them. He saw them as a picture of the wholeness of the mind.
66682.m: C. G. Jung saw the mandala as a picture of wholeness.

66683.q: In which country is Borobudur, a Buddhist temple in the shape of a mandala?
66683.e: Borobudur on the island of Java was built around the year 800. Seen from above, it looks like a huge mandala.
66683.m: Borobudur in Indonesia is a mandala made of stone.

66684.q: In which country is the temple complex of Angkor Wat?
66684.e: Angkor Wat is in the north-west of Cambodia, near the town of Siem Reap.

66685.q: Which figures are carved in great numbers into the walls of Angkor Wat?
66685.e: On the walls of Angkor Wat you can see almost 1800 figures of apsaras and devatas, which are heavenly dancers and goddesses.
66685.m: Angkor Wat is decorated with many figures of heavenly dancers.

66686.q: In which century was Angkor Wat built?
66686.e: Angkor Wat was built in the first half of the 12th century under King Suryavarman II.
66686.m: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century.

66687.e: Angkor was the capital of the Khmer Empire, which ruled large parts of Southeast Asia from the 9th to the 15th century.

66688.q: What surrounds the temple complex of Angkor Wat?
a: A high stone wall with cannons
66688.e: A moat about 190 metres wide surrounds the complex. It represents the world ocean.

66689.q: What is shown on the flag of Cambodia?
66689.e: Angkor Wat is the symbol of Cambodia. That is why the temple even appears on the national flag.
66689.m: Angkor Wat is on the flag of Cambodia.

66690.q: Measured by area, what is Angkor Wat considered to be?
a: The largest religious building in the world
The oldest church in the world
66690.e: With its moats and walls, Angkor Wat covers a huge area and is considered the largest religious building in the world.
66690.m: Angkor Wat is considered the largest religious building in the world.

66691.q: Which branch of Buddhism is the main one in Thailand?
66691.e: Over 90 per cent of people in Thailand are Buddhists, and most of them follow Theravada.
66691.m: Theravada Buddhism is the main branch in Thailand.

66692.q: What clothes do Buddhist monks wear in Thailand?
66692.e: Thai monks wear simple robes in orange or saffron yellow. They live by many strict rules.
66692.m: Monks in Thailand wear orange robes.

66693.q: What do Thai monks do on their alms round early in the morning?
66693.e: The monks walk barefoot through the streets. Believers put rice and other food into their bowls and so earn religious merit.
66693.m: On the alms round, monks receive their food from believers.

66694.q: Until what time of day are Theravada monks allowed to eat?
a: Only at six in the morning
66694.e: According to the rules, monks only eat between sunrise and midday. After that, only drinks are allowed.
66694.m: Theravada monks eat nothing after midday.

66695.q: What is common for many young men in Thailand?
a: To live as a monk for a while
To work on a ship for a year
To go on a pilgrimage to Mecca
To study abroad for a year
66695.e: Many men become monks for a few weeks or months. This is seen as an honour for the family and brings religious merit.
66695.m: Many Thai men live as monks for a while.

66696.q: What is a Buddhist monastery with a temple called in Thailand?
66696.e: A wat is a monastery complex with temples, living quarters for monks and often a school.
66696.m: In Thailand a Buddhist monastery is called a wat.

66697.q: Which famous figure is honoured in Wat Phra Kaew in Bangkok?
66697.e: Despite its name, the Emerald Buddha is a small green figure made of jade. It is considered the most important shrine in Thailand.
66697.m: The Emerald Buddha is the most important shrine in Thailand.

66698.q: How long does the rainy season retreat (Vassa), when monks stay in the monastery, last?
66698.e: During the rainy season, monks stay in one place for about three months and spend their time studying and meditating.
66698.m: The rainy season retreat lasts about three months.

66699.q: What should women in Thailand avoid doing to a monk?
66699.e: According to their rules, monks may not touch a woman. A woman therefore often hands over gifts on a cloth or puts them down.
66699.m: In Thailand, women do not touch monks.

66700.q: In which canton is the Tibet Institute Rikon?
66700.e: The institute is in Rikon in the Töss valley, part of the municipality of Zell in the canton of Zurich.
66700.m: The Tibet Institute is in Rikon in the canton of Zurich.

66701.q: Who was the Tibet Institute Rikon founded for?
66701.e: The Tibet Institute was opened in 1968. It was meant to help Tibetan refugees in Switzerland keep up their religion and culture.
66701.m: The Tibet Institute Rikon is there for the Tibetans in Switzerland.

66702.q: What is special about the Tibet Institute Rikon?
a: It is the first Tibetan monastery outside Asia
It is the seat of the Dalai Lama
It is the oldest temple in Europe
It is on the highest mountain in Switzerland
66702.e: The Tibet Institute Rikon is considered the first Tibetan Buddhist monastery outside Asia. A few monks live there with their abbot.
66702.m: Rikon has the first Tibetan monastery outside Asia.

66703.q: Where did many Tibetan refugees in Rikon find work?
a: In a factory for pans and cooking pots
66703.e: The Kuhn brothers ran a metalware factory in Rikon that makes pans and cooking pots. Many Tibetans found work there, and the brothers helped found the institute.
66703.m: In Rikon many Tibetans worked in a pan factory.

66704.q: Why did many people flee from Tibet from 1959 onwards?
a: They wanted to go skiing in Europe
66704.e: China occupied Tibet. After a failed uprising in 1959, many Tibetans fled, including the Dalai Lama. From 1961 Switzerland was one of the first Western countries to take in refugees.
66704.m: From 1959 many Tibetans fled from Chinese rule.

66705.q: Why was the monastery in Rikon officially called an “institute”?
a: The Federal Constitution banned new monasteries at that time
It was only a school without monks
The Dalai Lama wanted it that way
Only Christians were allowed to build monasteries
66705.e: The Federal Constitution of 1874 banned the founding of new monasteries. This ban was only lifted in 1973.
66705.m: Because of the ban on monasteries, the monastery in Rikon was called an “institute”.

66706.q: For what occasion did the Dalai Lama visit the Tibet Institute Rikon in 2018?
a: For the laying of the foundation stone
For the election of a new Dalai Lama
66706.e: In September 2018 the institute celebrated 50 years, and the 14th Dalai Lama came to Rikon.
66706.m: In 2018 the Tibet Institute Rikon celebrated its 50th anniversary.

66707.q: What is the library of the Tibet Institute Rikon known for?
a: One of the largest collections of Tibetan writings
66707.e: The library holds about 10,000 titles and is considered one of the largest collections about Tibet in the world.
66707.m: The library in Rikon keeps many Tibetan writings.

66708.q: How is the reading for the day chosen from the Guru Granth Sahib each morning?
a: The book is opened at random
The first page is always read
The oldest person chooses a favourite song
A page number is rolled with dice
66708.e: The book is opened at any place and the first passage is read aloud. It is seen as guidance for the day.
66708.m: The daily reading comes from a page opened at random.

66709.q: Since the last human guru, what have Sikhs regarded as their eternal guru?
66709.e: In 1708 the tenth guru decided that after him no person should be guru any more. Since then the scripture Guru Granth Sahib has been the eternal guru.
66709.m: The holy scripture is the eternal guru of the Sikhs.

66710.q: Which language do many Sikhs speak, which is also used in the texts of their holy scripture?
66710.e: The Sikh religion began in the Punjab in northern India. Many songs in the holy scripture are written in Punjabi.
66710.m: The language of many Sikhs is Punjabi.

66711.q: What does the Guru Granth Sahib mainly contain?
66711.e: The holy scripture of the Sikhs is mainly made up of hymns, which are religious songs. They are sung in the gurdwara.
66711.m: The Guru Granth Sahib mainly contains songs.

66712.q: What is special about the pages of all standard editions of the Guru Granth Sahib?
a: Each page has the same text in every copy
Each page has a different picture
66712.e: All standard editions have the same page layout with 1430 pages. So you find every passage in the same place in every book.
66712.m: All editions of the Guru Granth Sahib have the same page layout.

66713.q: Besides the hymns of the Sikh gurus, whose texts are in the Guru Granth Sahib?
66713.e: The Guru Granth Sahib also contains songs by saints such as Kabir or Baba Farid. They came from Hindu and Muslim traditions.
66713.m: The Guru Granth Sahib also contains songs by saints of other religions.

66714.q: How long does it take to read the whole Guru Granth Sahib aloud without a break?
66714.e: In a non-stop reading, several people take turns reading. It takes about 48 hours.
66714.m: A non-stop reading of the Sikh scripture takes about two days.

66715.q: What is waved over the Guru Granth Sahib during the reading as a sign of respect?
66715.e: A whisk made of animal hair, the chaur, is waved over the scripture. In the past this was a sign of honour for kings.
66715.m: The chaur is waved over the holy scripture out of respect.

66716.q: What does the K “Kesh” mean for Sikhs?
66716.e: Kesh means uncut hair. Many Sikhs let their hair and beard grow because they see the body as a gift from God.

66717.e: The kangha is a small comb made of wood. It stands for cleanliness and order.
66717.m: The kangha is a small wooden comb.

a: A bracelet made of steel or iron
66718.e: The kara is a simple bracelet made of steel or iron. Its round shape is a reminder of God, who has no beginning and no end.
66718.m: The kara is a steel bracelet.

66719.e: The kirpan is a small sword. It is a reminder of the duty to protect the weak and stand up for justice.
66719.m: The kirpan is a reminder to protect the weak.

66720.q: Why are the signs of faith of the Sikhs called “the Five Ks”?
a: They all begin with K in Punjabi
They are worn five times a day
66720.e: Kesh, kangha, kara, kirpan and kachera all begin with the sound K. Initiated Sikhs wear them as a sign of their faith.
66720.m: All of the Five Ks begin with the sound K.

66722.e: Khalsa means “pure”. This is the name of the community of initiated Sikhs.

66723.q: How many men were the first to be accepted when the Khalsa was founded?
66723.e: The first five are called the Panj Pyare, “the five beloved ones”. They were ready to give their lives for their faith.
66723.m: The first five members of the Khalsa are called the Panj Pyare.

66724.q: What name do male Sikhs take as a sign of the Khalsa, and what does it mean?
66724.e: Male Sikhs take the name Singh, which means “lion”. It was meant to show courage and remove differences between castes.

66725.q: What name do Sikh women receive as a sign of equality?
66725.e: Women take the name Kaur, which is often translated as “princess”. It stresses their dignity and equality.
66725.m: Sikh women take the name Kaur.

66726.q: What do Sikhs promise when they are accepted into the Khalsa?
a: To live by the rules of the Khalsa
66726.e: At the Amrit Sanchar ceremony, those being initiated drink sweetened water called amrit. They promise to live by the rules of the Khalsa.
66726.m: You are accepted into the Khalsa with the Amrit Sanchar ceremony.

66727.q: What is the sugar water stirred with at the Khalsa initiation?
66727.e: The sugar water is stirred with a double-edged sword called the khanda. The sword is also part of the Sikh symbol.
66727.m: At the initiation the water is stirred with a sword.

66728.q: In which present-day country is the place where the Khalsa was founded in 1699?
66728.e: The Khalsa was founded in 1699 in Anandpur Sahib in the Punjab. Today there is a large gurdwara there.
66728.m: The Khalsa was founded in India in 1699.

66729.e: Gurdwara is made up of “guru” and “dwara”, meaning gate or door. The holy scripture is kept in the gurdwara, and the community prays and sings there.
66729.m: Gurdwara means gateway to the guru.

66730.q: What is the free community kitchen in every gurdwara called?
66730.e: In the langar, all visitors get a free meal, whatever their background or religion. Everyone sits together on the floor.
66730.m: In the langar, everyone eats together for free.

66731.q: What must you do when you visit a gurdwara?
a: Cover your head and take off your shoes
66731.e: Out of respect, you cover your head and take off your shoes. Smoking and alcohol are forbidden.
66731.m: In a gurdwara you cover your head and go without shoes.

66732.q: What surrounds the Golden Temple of the Sikhs?
a: A high wall made of gold
66732.e: The Golden Temple stands in the middle of a large pool of water. Pilgrims bathe in it.
66732.m: The Golden Temple stands in a holy pool of water.

66733.q: How does the community sit in the gurdwara when praying and singing?
a: The rich at the front on chairs
Each family in its own room
66733.e: In the gurdwara everyone sits together on the floor, whatever their rank or background. The community is called the sangat.
66733.m: In the gurdwara everyone sits as equals on the floor.

66734.q: How can you recognise a gurdwara from far away?
66734.e: In front of every gurdwara flies a flag, usually orange, with the khanda symbol. It is called the Nishan Sahib.
66734.m: A flag flies in front of every gurdwara.

66735.q: In which Swiss town is the first gurdwara in Switzerland built in the traditional style?
66735.e: The gurdwara in Langenthal in the canton of Bern was finished in 2006. It was the first Sikh temple in Switzerland built in the traditional style.
66735.m: There is a large Sikh temple in Langenthal.

66736.e: Guru Nanak lived from 1469 to 1539 in the Punjab. He is the first of the ten gurus.
66736.m: Guru Nanak is the founder of Sikhism.

66737.q: In which region of South Asia did Sikhism begin?
66737.e: Sikhism began around 1500 in the Punjab, a region that today belongs to India and Pakistan. Punjab means “land of five rivers”.

66738.q: Which city with the Golden Temple was founded by the fourth Sikh guru, Ram Das?
66738.e: Guru Ram Das, the fourth guru, founded the city of Amritsar in the 16th century. He also had the holy pool of water built there.

66739.q: Which famous shrine did the fifth Sikh guru, Arjan, have built?
66739.e: Guru Arjan had the Harmandir Sahib, the Golden Temple in Amritsar, built. He was executed in 1606 and is seen as the first martyr of the Sikhs.
66739.m: Guru Arjan had the Golden Temple built.

66740.q: What did the two swords carried by the sixth Sikh guru, Hargobind, stand for?
66740.e: Guru Hargobind carried two swords called Miri and Piri. They stand for worldly and spiritual power.
66740.m: Guru Hargobind’s two swords stand for worldly and spiritual power.

66741.q: About how old was the eighth Sikh guru, Har Krishan, when he became guru?
66741.e: Guru Har Krishan became the eighth guru as a small child in 1661. He died of smallpox when he was only about eight years old.
66741.m: The youngest guru of the Sikhs was Guru Har Krishan.

66742.q: What did the ninth Sikh guru, Tegh Bahadur, stand up for before he was executed in 1675?
66742.e: Guru Tegh Bahadur stood up for persecuted Hindus. He was executed in 1675 on the orders of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
66742.m: Guru Tegh Bahadur died in 1675 for freedom of religion.

66743.q: What kind of festival was Vaisakhi originally in the Punjab?
66743.e: In the Punjab, Vaisakhi is an old harvest festival held when the wheat is ripe. It is also a New Year festival.
66743.m: Vaisakhi was originally a harvest festival.

66744.q: In which month is Vaisakhi celebrated?
66744.e: Vaisakhi usually falls on 13 or 14 April. The date follows the solar calendar.

66745.q: Which event do Sikhs especially remember at Vaisakhi?
a: The building of the Golden Temple
66745.e: At Vaisakhi in 1699, Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa. That is why the festival is especially important for Sikhs.
66745.m: At Vaisakhi, Sikhs celebrate the founding of the Khalsa.

66746.q: What do Sikhs often do in the streets at Vaisakhi?
66746.e: In the procession, called Nagar Kirtan, the community walks through the streets singing. Often five men in orange carrying swords lead the way.
66746.m: At Vaisakhi, Sikhs walk through the streets singing.

66747.q: What is often renewed in front of the gurdwara at Vaisakhi?
a: The flag and the cloth on the pole
66747.e: At Vaisakhi the flag in front of the gurdwara is taken down, the pole is washed and wrapped in new cloth. Then a new flag is raised.
66747.m: At Vaisakhi, the flagpole in front of the gurdwara gets new cloth.

66748.q: Which lively folk dance from the Punjab is often part of Vaisakhi?
66748.e: Bhangra is a powerful dance of the farmers in the Punjab. It is danced to drums at the harvest festival.
66748.m: Bhangra is a dance from the Punjab.

66749.q: Which grain is harvested in the Punjab around the time of Vaisakhi?
66749.e: In April the winter wheat in the Punjab is ripe. The farmers celebrate the end of the harvest.
66749.m: Wheat is harvested in the Punjab around the time of Vaisakhi.

66750.q: Who is seen as the most important teacher of Jainism in its present form?
66750.e: Mahavira lived in India in the 6th or 5th century BC. He gave Jainism its present form.
66750.m: Mahavira is the most important teacher of Jainism.

66751.e: Mahavira means “great hero”. It refers to victory over your own desires.

a: Not to harm any living being
66752.e: Mahavira taught ahimsa, non-violence towards all living beings. For Jains he is the last of 24 great teachers, the tirthankaras.
66752.m: Mahavira taught non-violence towards all living beings.

66753.q: Which other founder of a religion lived in India at about the same time as Mahavira?
66753.e: Mahavira and Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, both lived in north-eastern India. Both were against animal sacrifice.
66753.m: Mahavira and Buddha lived at the same time.

66754.q: What was Mahavira before he began wandering as an ascetic at about the age of 30?
66754.e: Mahavira’s real name was Vardhamana and he was a prince. He left his home and lived very strictly as a wandering ascetic for twelve years.

66755.q: What does the word “Jina”, from which the name Jainism comes, mean?
66755.e: Jina means “victor” or “conqueror”. It refers to someone who has defeated their passions.

66756.q: What colour do Shvetambara monks in Jainism wear?
66756.e: Shvetambara means “clad in white”. The other large group, the Digambaras, wear no clothes at all.

66757.q: What was the statue of Bahubali in India, about 17 metres tall, carved from?
66757.e: The statue in Shravanabelagola in the state of Karnataka was made around the year 981. It is an important place of pilgrimage for Jains.
66757.m: The huge Jain statue is carved from one block of granite.

66758.q: What are the three jewels of Jainism?
a: Right faith, right knowledge, right conduct
66758.e: The three jewels show the way to liberation. They include the right faith, the right knowledge and the right way of acting.

66759.q: Why do some Jain monks wear a cloth over their mouth?
a: So they do not breathe in tiny animals
66759.e: The mouth cloth is meant to stop small insects from being swallowed. In this way the monk protects even the tiniest living beings.
66759.m: The mouth cloth of Jain monks protects small animals.

66760.q: Why do Jain monks carry a small brush with them?
a: To sweep insects off the path
66760.e: With the soft brush they gently sweep insects aside before they sit down or walk. That way they do not tread on any animals.
66760.m: Jain monks gently sweep insects aside.

66761.q: Which foods do many strict Jains not eat?
a: Root vegetables such as onions and potatoes
66761.e: When root vegetables are dug up, many tiny creatures in the soil die and the whole plant is killed. That is why strict Jains do without them.
66761.m: Strict Jains do without root vegetables.

66762.q: What do Jains ask each other for at the end of their most important festival, Paryushana?
66762.e: Paryushana lasts eight to ten days with fasting. At the end, Jains ask others to forgive them for all their mistakes of the past year.
66762.m: At Paryushana, Jains ask for forgiveness.

66763.q: What does Jainism teach about truth?
a: It is written in just one book
66763.e: No person sees the whole truth, so you should respect other views. This teaching is called anekantavada.
66763.m: According to Jainism, truth has many sides.

66764.q: What is the goal of Jains when the soul is free of karma?
a: Liberation from the cycle of rebirth
66764.e: Jains believe in rebirth. When the soul has been cleansed of all karma, it is freed. This is called moksha.
66764.m: Jains aim for the liberation of the soul.

66765.e: Ahimsa literally means “not harming”. You should not cause harm to any living being.

66766.q: Which of the five great vows of Jain monks is seen as the most important?
66766.e: Jain monks take five great vows, for example truthfulness and owning nothing. The first and most important is not harming living beings.
66766.m: For Jains, ahimsa is the most important vow.

66767.q: Which Indian freedom fighter made ahimsa known around the world?
66767.e: Mahatma Gandhi fought without violence for India’s independence. He was also influenced by Jain friends.
66767.m: Gandhi fought non-violently for India’s freedom.

66768.q: Whose birthday is remembered on the International Day of Non-Violence on 2 October?
66768.e: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869. On this day the UN honours his non-violent struggle.
66768.m: The Day of Non-Violence is Gandhi’s birthday.

66769.q: Which way of eating follows for many people from the principle of ahimsa?
66769.e: If you do not want to harm any animal, you do not eat meat. That is why many Hindus, Jains and Buddhists are vegetarian.
66769.m: Ahimsa often leads to a vegetarian diet.

66770.q: In which religion from India do some monks wear a mouth cover so they do not swallow tiny animals?
66770.e: Jains take ahimsa, not harming, especially seriously. Some monks even sweep the path so they do not tread on any insects.
66770.m: Jains do not want to harm any living being.

66771.q: Which American civil rights campaigner fought non-violently against racial segregation in the 1950s and 1960s?
66771.e: Martin Luther King relied on non-violent resistance such as boycotts and marches. In 1959 he travelled to India to learn more about this method.
66771.m: Martin Luther King fought non-violently for civil rights.

66772.e: Baha'u'llah lived from 1817 to 1892. His name means “glory of God”.
66772.m: Baha'u'llah is the founder of the Baha'i faith.

66773.q: In which country did the Baha'i religion begin in the 19th century?
66773.e: The Baha'i religion began in the middle of the 19th century in Persia, today’s Iran. Baha'is are still persecuted there today.
66773.m: The Baha'i religion comes from Persia.

66774.q: What does the title “Bab” of the forerunner of the Baha'i religion mean?
66774.e: Bab is an Arabic word meaning “gate”. From 1844 the Bab announced that a messenger of God would come. He was executed in 1850.
66774.m: The Bab was the forerunner of Baha'u'llah.

66775.q: Which principle does the Baha'i religion particularly stress?
a: The separation of men and women
66775.e: Baha'is believe that all people are one family. They also stress that men and women are of equal worth.
66775.m: Baha'is stress the unity of humankind.

66776.q: How many sides does a Baha'i House of Worship have?
66776.e: Every House of Worship has nine sides and nine entrances. In the Baha'i faith the number nine stands for perfection.
66776.m: A Baha'i House of Worship has nine sides.

66777.q: Where is the only Baha'i House of Worship in Europe so far?
66777.e: The House of Worship in Hofheim-Langenhain near Frankfurt am Main was opened in 1964. It is open to all visitors.
66777.m: Europe’s Baha'i House of Worship is near Frankfurt.

66778.q: When do Baha'is celebrate their New Year festival, Naw-Ruz?
66778.e: Naw-Ruz falls at the start of spring, around 21 March. Before it, Baha'is fast during the day for 19 days.
66778.m: The Baha'i New Year is at the start of spring.

66779.q: In which country are the famous Baha'i Gardens of Haifa?
66779.e: Haifa is a port city in the north of Israel. The world centre of the Baha'is is there.
66779.m: The Baha'i Gardens are in Haifa in Israel.

66780.q: On which mountain are the terraced gardens of the Baha'is in Haifa?
66780.e: The gardens stretch up Mount Carmel. From the top you can see over the city and the Mediterranean Sea.
66780.m: The Baha'i Gardens are on Mount Carmel.

66781.q: How are the Baha'i Gardens in Haifa laid out?
a: As a flat park on the beach
As a garden on a rooftop
As a maze in a cave
66781.e: The gardens stretch up Mount Carmel in many terraces and are about one kilometre long.
66781.m: The Baha'i Gardens are laid out in terraces on the mountain.

66782.q: What crowns the shrine in the middle of the Baha'i Gardens in Haifa?
66782.e: In the middle of the terraces stands a shrine with a golden dome. It is one of the landmarks of Haifa.
66782.m: The shrine in the Baha'i Gardens has a golden dome.

66783.q: Which famous list includes the holy places of the Baha'is in Haifa?
a: List of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
66783.e: In 2008 UNESCO added the holy places of the Baha'is in Haifa and Western Galilee to the World Heritage List.
66783.m: The Baha'i sites in Haifa are UNESCO World Heritage.

66784.q: What can you see from the top of the Baha'i Gardens on Mount Carmel?
a: The city of Haifa and the Mediterranean Sea
66784.e: Haifa lies on the Mediterranean. From the upper terraces you look over the city and the harbour out to the sea.
66784.m: The Baha'i Gardens offer a view over Haifa and the Mediterranean.

66785.q: Why is Haifa important for Baha'is?
a: Their only house of prayer is there
66785.e: The world centre of the Baha'is is in Haifa. Their highest governing body also has its seat there.
66785.m: The world centre of the Baha'is is in Haifa.

66786.q: Who is seen as the founder of Zoroastrianism?
66786.e: Zarathustra was a prophet in ancient Iran. In Greek he is called Zoroaster, which is where the name Zoroastrianism comes from.
66786.m: Zarathustra is the founder of Zoroastrianism.

66787.q: What is the name of the highest god in Zoroastrianism?
66787.e: Ahura Mazda means “wise lord”. He is the creator and goodness itself.
66787.m: The highest god of the Zoroastrians is Ahura Mazda.

66788.q: What is the most important motto of Zoroastrianism?
a: Good thoughts, good words, good deeds
66788.e: In Avestan these three principles are called humata, hukhta and hvarshta. Every person should freely choose what is good.
66788.m: Zoroastrians strive for good thoughts, words and deeds.

66789.q: What is the collection of holy scriptures of the Zoroastrians called?
66789.e: The Avesta is written in an old Iranian language. For a long time it was passed on only by word of mouth.
66789.m: The holy scripture of the Zoroastrians is called the Avesta.

66790.q: In which present-day country did Zarathustra live?
66790.e: Zarathustra was a prophet in ancient Iran, which used to be called Persia. Seventeen songs, the Gathas, are said to be his.

66791.q: What is the name of Ahura Mazda’s evil opponent?
66791.e: Angra Mainyu, later called Ahriman, stands for evil and destruction. In the struggle between good and evil, people should choose good.

66793.q: What plays a particularly important role in Zoroastrian temples?
66793.e: A sacred fire burns in Zoroastrian temples. It is a sign of purity and of the god Ahura Mazda.
66793.m: The sacred fire is very important in Zoroastrianism.

66794.q: What does fire stand for in Zoroastrianism?
66794.e: Fire is a sign of purity and of the light of God. Zoroastrians do not worship fire as a god.
66794.m: For Zoroastrians, fire is a sign of purity.

66795.q: What burns in a Zoroastrian fire temple?
a: A sacred fire that should never go out
A fire only on feast days
66795.e: In the fire temple a sacred fire burns without a break. Priests keep it burning day and night.
66795.m: The sacred fire in the fire temple should never go out.

66796.q: Who looks after the sacred fire in the fire temple?
66796.e: Priests add wood day and night and keep the fire pure. So it burns without a break.
66796.m: Priests guard the sacred fire in the fire temple.

66797.q: Which wood do the priests often put on the sacred fire?
66797.e: Sandalwood smells pleasant and is offered to the fire as a gift. Visitors often bring sandalwood too.
66797.m: The sacred fire is fed with sandalwood.

66798.q: Why do priests wear a cloth over their mouth in front of the sacred fire?
a: So their breath does not make the fire impure
So they do not have to talk
66798.e: The cloth is called a padan. It stops breath or saliva from touching the pure fire.
66798.m: Priests protect the sacred fire with a mouth cloth.

66799.q: In which country are there old Zoroastrian fire temples whose fire is said to have burned for centuries?
66799.e: Zoroastrianism comes from ancient Persia, today’s Iran. In the city of Yazd a fire has been burning for about 1500 years.
66799.m: Famous fire temples are in Iran.

66800.q: In which country do most Parsis, the Zoroastrians who once emigrated from Persia, live?
66800.e: The Parsis fled from Persia to India more than 1000 years ago. Their most important fire temples are there today.
66800.m: The Parsis live mainly in India.

66801.e: The Parsis are descendants of Zoroastrians who emigrated from Persia to India. The name means “Persians”.
66801.m: The Parsis are Zoroastrians in India.

66802.q: Why did the ancestors of the Parsis leave Persia?
a: Because of persecution after the Islamic conquest
Because of an outbreak of disease in India
66802.e: After the Arab Islamic conquest of Persia in the 7th century, Zoroastrians were put under more and more pressure. Some fled across the sea to western India.
66802.m: The ancestors of the Parsis fled from Persia to India.

66803.q: In which city does the largest community of Parsis live today?
66803.e: Most Parsis live in Mumbai, formerly Bombay. They have shaped the city strongly through trade and industry.

66804.q: Which famous rock singer of the band Queen came from a Parsi family?
66804.e: Freddie Mercury’s real name was Farrokh Bulsara and he was born in Zanzibar in 1946. His parents were Parsis.
66804.m: Freddie Mercury came from a Parsi family.

66805.q: Which famous Indian business family is Parsi?
66805.e: In the 19th century Jamsetji Tata founded the Tata Group, today one of India’s largest companies. The family is of Parsi origin.
66805.m: The Tata business family is Parsi.

66806.q: What does a Parsi child receive at the Navjote initiation ceremony?
a: A white shirt and a sacred cord
66806.e: At the Navjote the child receives the shirt called sudreh and the cord called kusti. With them, the child is welcomed into the community.
66806.m: At the Navjote a child receives a shirt and a cord.

66807.q: What are the buildings called where Parsis traditionally leave their dead to the vultures?
66807.e: The Towers of Silence are called dakhma. The dead should not make earth or fire impure, so they are neither buried nor burned.
66807.m: Parsis traditionally lay their dead in Towers of Silence.

66808.q: In which country did Confucius live?
66808.e: Confucius was born in 551 BC in the small state of Lu in eastern China. His home town is the city of Qufu.

66809.q: Who collected and wrote down the sayings of Confucius?
66809.e: The “Analects” contain sayings and short conversations of Confucius. His students and their students collected them.
66809.m: The students of Confucius collected his sayings.

66810.q: According to the teaching of Confucius, what should children show their parents?
66810.e: This virtue is called xiao: children should respect their parents, obey them and look after them in old age. In Confucianism it is seen as the basis of society.
66810.m: Xiao is children’s deep respect for their parents.

66811.q: Which virtue did Confucius see as the highest?
66811.e: Confucius called it ren: humaneness or kindness towards other people. A noble person should show it in everything.
66811.m: In Confucianism, ren stands for humaneness and kindness.

66812.q: What was Confucius’s main job, which made him famous?
66812.e: Confucius taught many students, about 3000 according to tradition. He wanted not only nobles but all talented people to be able to learn.
66812.m: Confucius became famous as the teacher of many students.

66813.q: For about how long did Confucianism shape China as the state philosophy?
66813.e: Under the Han dynasty, Confucianism became the official state philosophy in the 2nd century BC. After that it shaped China for about 2000 years.
66813.m: Confucianism shaped China for about 2000 years.

66814.q: What did officials in imperial China have to know well for the state exams for a long time?
66814.e: Anyone who wanted to become an official had to know and explain the Confucian writings in difficult exams. These exams were only abolished in 1905.
66814.m: For centuries, Chinese officials were tested on the Confucian writings.

66815.q: Which relationship is one of the five most important relationships in Confucianism?
66815.e: The five relationships are: ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife, older and younger brother, and friend and friend. In each relationship, each side has duties.
66815.m: Confucianism orders society by five basic relationships.

66816.q: What does the name Laozi roughly mean?
66816.e: “Lao” means old and “zi” is a title of honour for a master or teacher. So Laozi is more of an honorary name than a real personal name.

66817.q: About how long ago is Laozi said to have lived?
66817.e: Tradition makes Laozi an older contemporary of Confucius in the 6th century BC. However, some experts date the texts said to be his to a later time.
66817.m: Laozi is said to have lived about 2500 years ago.

66818.q: According to legend, on which animal does Laozi ride out of China?
66818.e: The legend says that the old Laozi left China heading west on a water buffalo. That is why many Chinese pictures show him on a buffalo.
66818.m: In the legend, Laozi rides west on a water buffalo.

66819.q: According to legend, who asked Laozi to write down his teaching?
66819.e: When Laozi wanted to leave the country, the guard at the border pass, Yin Xi, asked him to write down his wisdom. That is how the famous book is said to have come about.
66819.m: A border guard is said to have persuaded Laozi to write his book.

66820.q: Which teaching goes back to Laozi?
66820.e: Laozi is seen as the founder of Daoism. He is said to have been an archivist at the royal court of the Zhou.
66820.m: Laozi is seen as the founder of Daoism.

66821.q: According to old accounts, which famous thinker is Laozi said to have met?
66821.e: Old Chinese texts tell of a meeting between the older Laozi and the younger Confucius. Nobody knows whether this meeting really took place.
66821.m: According to tradition, Laozi and Confucius met.

66822.q: How is Laozi honoured in religious Daoism?
66822.e: In religious Daoism, Laozi was made into a god and is worshipped under the name Taishang Laojun. That is why there are figures of him in Daoist temples.
66822.m: In religious Daoism, Laozi is worshipped as a god.

66823.q: Why is so little known for certain about Laozi’s life?
a: He lived in secret in Japan
66823.e: There is hardly any reliable information about Laozi, mainly legends. Some experts think he is an invented figure or one made up of several people.
66823.m: What we know about Laozi comes mainly from legends.
